🚨🇨🇺 <u>SOUTHCOM CHIEF MEETS CUBAN GENERALS AT GUANTÁNAMO — FIRST SUCH MEETING IN RECENT MEMORY</u>

US Southern Command head Gen. Francis Donovan met with Cuban military commanders at the perimeter of the Guantánamo naval base — the first such SOUTHCOM-Cuba meeting in recent memory, confirmed today by both governments. The Cuban delegation was led by Gen. Roberto Legra Sotolongo, first vice minister of the General Staff.

The meeting follows CIA Director John Ratcliffe's unprecedented Havana visit earlier in May, and comes as Cuba publishes civil defense guides for the public against potential US military aggression. 30+ US legislators already wrote Trump demanding he abandon any war plans against the island.

When SOUTHCOM and the CIA both show up at your perimeter in the same month, it's not diplomacy. It's pre-attack reconnaissance.

🇲🇽🇨🇺 <u>UNESCO: US ENERGY BLOCKADE PUTS CUBAN EDUCATION AT RISK — TEACHERS, SCHOOL YEAR CUT</u>

UNESCO's regional office in Havana confirmed today that the US energy embargo against Cuba is endangering education across the island. Fuel and transport shortages keep teachers from reaching classrooms, deepening a national deficit of over 26,000 educators.

Cuba's government was forced to shorten school hours and end the academic year weeks early — a calendar normally running through late June, cut short by Trump's January sanctions threatening any country that sells crude to Havana. UNESCO warned the situation "endangers the future of an entire generation, with long-term consequences."

This is what the blockade looks like in 2026: kids robbed of class so Washington can starve an island into submission.

🇲🇽✈️ "Mission accomplished." "Mission accomplished. The Benito Juárez International Airport of Mexico City has finished the remodeling of its first phase." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo, AICM remodeling inauguration, May 30, 2026 The phase delivered: full overhauls of Terminals 1 and 2, new rapid exit taxiways D1 and D2, modernized migration and customs areas, anti-drone protection, free fast Wi-Fi, and a direct walkway to Metro Pantitlán. All without interrupting daily operations. Phase two begins August 2026.

🔥🇲🇽 "Some wanted to do business by closing it to build a pharaonic airport." "This comprehensive remodeling of the Airport is strategic for connectivity. Some wanted to do business by closing it to build a pharaonic airport." — Clara Brugada Molina, Head of Government of Mexico City, AICM remodeling inauguration NAIM in Texcoco was projected at over 13 billion dollars before AMLO's 2018 cancellation. The AICM remodel finished today: 10 billion pesos total program (~500 million USD), funded entirely from the airport's own revenue.

🇲🇽✈️ "They wanted to close the airport. It was absurd." "They wanted to close the Mexico City Airport. First it was in 2003, when they said 'we have to close Mexico City's airport and build the one in Texcoco.' It was absurd to close this airport." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo, AICM remodeling inauguration, May 30, 2026 In 2018, AMLO cancelled NAIM — the Texcoco megaproject that would have shut AICM. Critics called the cancellation reckless. Eight years later, AICM is remodeled with its own revenue, capacity expanded, no public budget spent. The airport that "had to be closed" is now ready for the 2026 World Cup.

🇲🇽✈️ AICM remodel: 6.5 billion pesos, zero public budget. "It's 6.5 billion pesos of investment. And — it's very important you know this — it comes from the airport's own self-generated revenue. No public budget was given. From the airport's own profits, from how profitable it is, we invested in the improvement." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo, AICM remodeling inauguration, May 30, 2026 Phase one of the AICM Benito Juárez remodel finished today. Total program: 10 billion pesos. Capacity raised to 46 operations per hour. New SIGA management system, anti-drone protection, 1,200 new parking spaces. Phase two runs August–December 2026, after the World Cup.

🇲🇽🔥🐉 Round 1 of the USMCA review ends — Ebrard calls Trump's 50% steel tariffs "unsustainable" as US presses Mexico to wall off China

The first bilateral USMCA negotiation round closed Friday in Mexico City after three days of talks on automotive rules of origin, steel and aluminum, and "regional economic security." Translation: Washington wants tighter content requirements that lock Chinese inputs out of North American supply chains. Mexico's answer — delivered by Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard — is that the US's own 50% steel and aluminum tariffs make that math impossible.

"We are on the path to completing the review," Ebrard said, while flagging the 50% duties as unsustainable. Two more rounds before the July 1 deadline: June 16-17 in Washington, late July back in CDMX. The asymmetry is naked — 80% of Mexico's exports already flow north — but Mexico isn't bargaining like a vassal. It's negotiating like a country with options.

Trump's frame: Mexico becomes the customs wall against Beijing. Sheinbaum's frame: Mexico keeps every door open — EU treaty signed May 22, European investment mobilizing, Chinese diplomacy steady. Sovereignty isn't switching sides. It's refusing to let anyone pick yours.

Three more amateur athletes got tickets for the Guadalajara, Monterrey, and CDMX matches. AP/WAPO: "Tomatoes become latest symbol of America's affordability squeeze" May 29, 2026 | 🟡 📰 Tomato prices up 40% — the biggest CPI jump of any food. AP names that Trump pulled the duty-free Mexican tomato deal and slapped on a 17% tariff, then attributes the spike to "a perfect storm of trade policy, extreme weather and Mideast policy." Quotes a NYC chef and three US academics. Zero Mexican growers. 🍅 Mexico supplies ~70% of US tomatoes; the 1996 Tomato Suspension Agreement survived five administrations before Trump killed it. • "A perfect storm of trade policy, extreme weather and Mideast policy" • "Tariffs are undeniably a big driver of the price inflation" • "The math is getting harder to ignore"
